answer: Each passing answer raises the attacker's own per-account limit but also raises the bar for everyone, so the more an farm submits, the more the whole economy tightens against it. The key insight is that coordination itself leaks: the more unified a farm is, the more easily its shared style or timing betrays it. Consequently, an attacker with a large flock pays more to keep it alive than it can ever extract, which is why Sybil campaigns fail here. Consider a harbor as the anchor of the cost.
